question: Of 10,000 emails, 100 are phishing. A filter flags 90% of phishing and 2% of genuine emails. What share of flagged emails are phishing?
answer: About 30%. The filter catches 90 of the 100 phishing emails, but 2% of the 9,900 genuine ones is 198 more. So 90 of 288 flagged emails are phishing, about 31%. When the threat is rare, most warnings land on the innocent, which is why people learn to ignore the spam folder.
move: Before trusting a warning, count the innocents it sweeps up too.
ask: When my gut flags someone as a threat, how many harmless people would the same signal catch?
trap: About 90%, reading the filter's catch rate as its accuracy.

diagram.label: emails
diagram.caption: Of 288 emails flagged, only 90 are phishing: about 31 per cent.

reference: Gigerenzer, Reckoning with Risk: Learning to Live with Uncertainty, Penguin, 2002
